Consult Summary:
- Telehealth consult for activity-related right knee pain and clicking for ~2 weeks in a marathon-training patient; conservative measures advised, physiotherapy referral arranged, and a stronger anti-inflammatory prescribed.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Knee pain and clicking, worse with running; concern for injury.
- Symptom details:
  - Onset/duration: ~2 weeks, began after increasing running for marathon training.
  - Location: Predominantly right knee; pain felt centrally, sometimes to the right side of the knee.
  - Triggers/progression: Pain starts ~20 minutes into runs (~2.5–3 miles); recent runs required stopping due to worsening pain. Clicking noted during gym/ab exercises with knee flexion/extension. Initial mild swelling after first run improved with ice; currently no swelling or pain at rest.
  - Associated symptoms: One episode of tingling in right toes after a run, resolved; occasional mild lower leg sock-line indentations after prolonged standing.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No giving way/instability, no locking, no problems with stairs or walking, no persistent swelling, no color or temperature changes in lower legs, no calf pain, no back pain, no foot/arch pain. Full ability to fully flex and extend the knee.
- Past medical history:
  - Farsighted; prior LASIK surgery.
  - Past severe UTI episode (evaluated in ER; kidney stones suspected at the time).
  - Sports: prior ice hockey fall with large bruise a few months ago; no ongoing issues reported.
- Medications:
  - Ibuprofen up to 400 mg as needed.
  - Aleve (naproxen) — dose/route/frequency not documented; patient uncertain about drug class.
  - Vitamin D — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Melatonin — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Xanax (alprazolam) occasionally for sleep — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Social history:
  - Currently training for a marathon; runs up to ~7–8 miles; goes to the gym several times per week.
  - Occasional cannabis use (“smoke a joint”).
- Preventive care: Not discussed.

Examination:
- 

Impression:
- Activity-related right knee pain with clicking, likely overuse; requires in-person assessment to evaluate for structural causes (e.g., cartilage pathology). ACL injury cannot be confirmed or excluded via video.

Plan:
- Conservative care:
  - Continue ice therapy as much as feasible.
  - Reduce running volume/intensity; avoid running through significant pain.
- Medications:
  - Prescribed a stronger anti-inflammatory to take regularly with food; do not take concurrently with ibuprofen (name/dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Referrals:
  - Physiotherapy referral placed for comprehensive knee assessment.
- Further evaluation:
  - Consider imaging to assess intra-articular structures (e.g., cartilage) based on physiotherapy/clinical findings.
  - Option for clinic evaluation if physiotherapy wait time is prolonged.
- Safety net/return precautions:
  - Seek urgent care if persistent swelling, warmth/redness of the knee, fever/systemic illness, or if the knee locks and cannot bend/straighten.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements:
  - Allergies not documented.
  - Full medication reconciliation (names/doses/routes/frequencies) incomplete.
  - No vitals or physical examination performed.
  - Past medical, surgical, family history limited; social history (tobacco/alcohol) not documented.
● Internal conflicts:
  - Patient initially reported “knees” hurting and clicking; later clarified pain is in the right knee (conflict noted).
  - Patient uncertain about Aleve’s drug class (naproxen); potential confusion noted.
● Transcript quality:
  - Generally clear; minor filler words; no significant audio issues reported.
